stories.title: BJP held an edge as Karnataka contests became increasingly bipolar
stories.summary: Election data reviewed by The Hindu shows that 77 percent of Karnataka Assembly seats had effectively bipolar contests in 2018, with the BJP holding an advantage in many such races. The analysis describes a structural shift toward two leading competitors despite the state's multi-party landscape. It does not establish that the same pattern will persist in later elections.
stories.why_it_matters: More two-way contests change vote-transfer incentives, alliance calculations and the threshold needed to win, shaping how parties nominate candidates and target constituencies throughout Karnataka.
stories.evidence_status: The Hindu provides the 77-percent measure and electoral interpretation; the underlying constituency dataset is not separately supplied and future applicability is uncertain.

confidence.rationale: Specific facts are attributed to the supplied reporting, while missing records, responses and later outcomes remain explicit.

coverage.rationale: One supplied reporting desk covers this event, with limited independent follow-up in the available material.
